draft.briefing: Hey, you're in Madurai! This city on the Vaigai has more than 2,500 years of recorded history, and even Megasthenes, the Greek ambassador to the Mauryas, wrote about it. Locals call it Thoongaa Nagaram, the city that never sleeps.
draft.hungryLine: Madurai food is the real taste of Tamil Nadu, so try jigarthanda, kuzhi paniyaram and appam with mutton paya, and if you can handle heat, hit an evening mutton stall.

moodReplies.show-me-around: The Meenakshi Temple is a 15 min walk, Simmakkal with its stone lion is 13 minutes, and the Koodal Azhagar Temple is about 21 minutes away.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Cool off with a tall jigarthanda at the Famous Jigarthanda shop on the way from the Meenakshi Temple to the Thirumalai Nayak Palace.
moodReplies.surprise-me: Murugan Idly Shop is so loved here that it has opened branches in the UK and Singapore.

spots.name: Meenakshi Temple
spots.detail: 15 min walk · The great Meenakshi Sundareswarar temple on the Vaigai's south bank

spots.name: Simmakkal
spots.detail: 13 min walk · Neighbourhood named after its stone lion statue

spots.name: Koodal Azhagar Temple
spots.detail: 21 min walk · One of the 108 Divya Desams, with a five-tiered gopuram

legends.title: The lion at the gate
legends.body: When the British collector pulled down three of the old city walls, the landmark at the North Veli Street gate was replaced with a stone lion found near Thirumalai Naicker Mahal. The whole area around it took its name, Simmakkal, the stone lion.

legends.title: The old night market
legends.body: Yanaikkal is named after a stone elephant. Hundreds of years ago this area was called Allankadi, a market busy with trade through the night.

tips.title: Catch Brahmotsavam in May to June.
tips.body: Koodal Azhagar Temple holds its 14-day Brahmotsavam festival in the Tamil month of Vaikasi.

tips.title: Ease into the spice.
tips.body: If you're not used to the heat, start with a kotthu parotta made without chillies or pepper before you try the mutton stalls.

story.title: Pandyan capital
story.body: The Pandyan capital was at Korkai and was later moved to Koodal, today's Madurai, under Nedunj Cheliyan I. The third Tamil Sangam of scholars is said to have met here.

story.title: Roman trade
story.body: Digs at Keezhadi near Madurai show settlements and Roman trade links going back to 300 BCE. Megasthenes and Kautilya both mention the city.

story.title: The temple rises
story.body: The Pandyas built the early Meenakshi Temple in the 12th and 13th centuries. After the Delhi Sultanate's armies destroyed it, the Vijayanagara Empire rebuilt it in the 14th century.

story.title: The Nayaks
story.body: The Madurai Nayaks expanded the temple hugely. Thirumalai Nayak built his palace in the 17th century, though only a quarter of it survives.

story.title: City that never sleeps
story.body: The Madurai Municipal Corporation was set up on 1 November 1866. Today Madurai is called the cultural capital of Tamil Nadu.
